To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) TrkB regulates hippocampal neuroplasticity; (ii) TrkB regulates behavioral responses to ADs; (iii) TrkB regulates proliferation and differentiation of hippocampal NPCs; and (iv) TrkB regulates the response to exercise.

1) the receptor tyrosin kinase TrkB is required for proliferation and neuronal differentiation of hippocampal progenitor cells, 2) mice lacking TrkB in hippocampus progenitors display impaired proliferation and differentiation, and 3) TrkB is essential for behavioral sensitivity to antidepressant drugs.

TrkB is essential in adult hippocampal neural progenitors to promote proliferation and neurogenesis, to render mice behaviorally sensitive to chronic ADs and voluntary exercise, and that this cell-autonomous function is lost in TrkB mutants lacking the TrkB receptor in differentiated DG neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular regulation of adult neurogenesis in the dentate region of the hippocampus and its functional implications for behavior and mood.
the identification and functional characterization of the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the formation and function of the hippocampal neurogenic niche.
the identification of molecular mechanisms regulating adult hippocampal neuroplasticity and its impact on behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TrkB is a critical regulator of hippocampal neurogenic niche, and that its ablation renders mice behaviorally insensitive and unresponsive to antidepressive treatment.
the absence of the TrkB receptor in NPCs of the dentate gyruss results in a reduction of neurogenesis, and that this is the cause of the lack of response to antidepressant treatment.
the absence of TrkB in NPCs in the hippocampal DG results in an impairment of proliferation and neurogenesis, which renders mice behaviorally insensitive when exposed to chronic AD treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TrkB regulates adult hippocampal neurogenic niche, and TrkB in NPCs regulates neurogenic niche and TrkB in mature neurons regulate neuronal function.
TrkB is essential for the regulation of neurogenesis, and that TrkB is also essential for the regulation behavioral sensitivity to antidepressants.
the neurotrophin receptor TrkB regulates hippocampal neurogenetic activity and governs the response to antidepressant treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

TrkB signaling in adult neural progenitor cells (i.e., in the hippocampal dentate gyrus) is essential for the proliferation and neuronal differentiation of neural progenitor cells, and that TrkB in these progenitor cells regulates the behavioral sensitivity to chronic antidepressant treatment in depression- or anxiety-like paradigams.
TrkB is a key regulator of hippocampal neuroplasticity and that TrkB is essential for the behavioral response to antidepressive treatment.
TrkB is a key regulator of neurogenesis and behavioral responses to antidepressive drugs.
